access_note: The library is free, but the developers state that only the commercial tool Dymola fully supports it.
description: The TransiEnt Library is a Modelica library for the simulation of coupled energy networks, as its load script describes it, developed in the research projects TransiEnt.EE, ResiliEntEE, IntegraNet and IntegraNet II, which were supported by the German Federal Ministry of Economics and Energy. The research team consists of three institutes of Hamburg University of Technology (Engineering Thermodynamics, Energy Systems, and Electrical Power and Energy Technology), Fraunhofer UMSICHT, the Gas- und Wärme-Institut Essen and XRG Simulation. It builds on the ClaRa library for Clausius-Rankine cycles, which users download separately (version 1.8.1), the TILMedia media library and, for some components, the Modelica Buildings Library. The library is location-independent: systems of any region or city are assembled from its components. Code is on GitHub (version 2.0.3 in the README, tag v3.0.0) under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost. Caveats: according to its README only Dymola fully supports TransiEnt; all models were tested with Dymola 2025x Refresh 1, and the superstructure models work fully only up to Dymola 2023, so users of free Modelica tools may meet problems; the README also warns that the development version may contain bugs and points to the stable release. Simulation uses are dynamic network flow and resilience studies of integrated energy systems and optimisation of their design. Related records: it compares with model-openipsl, another Modelica library for power systems.
